A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and retain the central theorem and earlier constructions. Their complete text, equations and figures are readable, including v3's Appendix A; v2 has no appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports mathematical constructions and proofs, with no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V3 remains theoretical throughout, including the new group-convolutional example and Appendix A. No original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: V3 Section 6 adds a formal depth-n group-convolutional network construction using group-transformed feature maps, their composition and integration. It introduces a corresponding ridgelet transform computed from the target function at the group identity. This substantially extends the explicit model constructions while retaining the earlier fully connected and quadratic-form models.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts task evaluations. The added group-convolutional construction expands theoretical model coverage, not evaluated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. V3 mentions DeepSets and E(n)-equivariant maps as theoretical examples, not as experimentally compared baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness evaluations or empirical case studies. The additional mathematical examples and proofs are theoretical developments.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical numerical results, rankings or observational findings. The new reconstruction statements are formal theoretical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V3 Section 6 introduces the equivariant target-function space, convolutional construction, Lemma 6 and Theorem 5 with proofs. Remark 2 adds assertions concerning reducible and dual representations. Appendix A adds an explicit proof of parameter-space representation unitarity; the other appendix proofs match relocated v2 proofs. The central Theorem 4 is substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claim of unified constructive universality is retained. The abstract and contribution list now explicitly include depth-n group-convolutional networks, and the introduction identifies constructing irreducible representations as a contribution. The earlier fully connected and quadratic-form claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands interpretation and applicability discussion: Section 3.1.1 and Remark 2 introduce fiber-bundle and section interpretations, explain the asymmetric irreducibility requirement, and discuss zero or divergent reconstruction constants and case-specific regularity requirements. Section 6 additionally explains identity-element encoding and the role and limitations of the auxiliary group.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation instructions, experimental hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes or code/data access information. The new formulas specify mathematical constructions rather than implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: V3 adds Sonoda and Murata (2017a), 'Neural network with unbounded activation functions is universal approximator,' for the activation-function discussion. Section 6 explicitly positions the new construction as extending the already-cited depth-2 GCN ridgelet work to depth-n, contrasting its assumptions with the Fourier approach. The broader literature positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 revises the abstract and contributions, divides Section 3.1 into interpretation and construction subsections, reorganizes explanatory paragraphs, and moves existing proofs into Appendix A. These are localized revisions; most introductory background, preliminaries, the main proof, earlier examples and discussion retain their wording and order.

P2.justification: V3 adds the geometric Figure 2, retains Figure 1, and renumbers the earlier deep-network diagram from Figure 2 to Figure 3. Smaller body text and relocated material change pagination and figure placement, while the single-column layout remains. Neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: The worked GCN construction and reconstruction proof make the framework's application more explicit than in v2, while Remark 2 clarifies important regularity and nondegeneracy limitations. This improves explanatory completeness without resolving those case-specific requirements. Small new inconsistencies, including Figure 2 labeling its base X while the text and diagram use Y^X, slightly offset the clarity gains.
